title: Gluing mixed Weil filtrations across a reduced frontier chain
statement:
Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$, as in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, let $\mathcal F$ be a constructible Weil sheaf of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and let $r:(X_0)_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X_0$ be the reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Suppose a finite chain of reduced closed $k_0$-subschemes is given,
$$Z_0=(X_0)_{\mathrm{red}}\supset Z_1\supset\cdots\supset Z_t=\varnothing,$$
and for each $a<t$ its open difference $U_a=Z_a\setminus Z_{a+1}$ is a finite disjoint union of open and closed $k_0$-subschemes $U_{a,b}$. All inclusions and this decomposition are defined over $k_0$. Suppose the restriction of $\mathcal F$ to every $U_{a,b}$ has a finite mixed Weil filtration. Then $\mathcal F$ has a finite mixed Weil filtration; if all the component filtrations have weights at most a given real $w$, so does the resulting filtration.

The open extension-by-zero of each component filtration is a filtration by constructible Weil subsheaves with the same pure quotient weights. The restrictions $\mathcal F_a=\mathcal F|_{Z_a}$ fit, for the open $j_a:U_a\hookrightarrow Z_a$ and closed $i_a:Z_{a+1}\hookrightarrow Z_a$, into Weil-equivariant short exact sequences
$$0\longrightarrow j_{a!}(\mathcal F_a|_{U_a})\longrightarrow\mathcal F_a\longrightarrow i_{a*}\mathcal F_{a+1}\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $j_{a!}$ is the compact-support direct image of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], $i_{a*}$ and $r_*$ are direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image], restrictions and $r^*$ are inverse images of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], all with their induced Weil structures; $j_{a!}$ and $i_{a*}$ are exact on the constructible hearts and preserve mixed filtrations with their upper weight bounds. The reduction unit is a Weil isomorphism $\mathcal F\cong r_*r^*\mathcal F$ in the heart. The conclusion includes the empty scheme, the zero sheaf, empty component sets and nonreduced $X_0$; no reality hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Apply immersion/reduction filtration transport to each closed inclusion and to the reduction. Package its canonical derived carrier, adjunction and normalized unit as ZlFrontierClosedImage. Its exact image functors preserve each pure quotient with its assigned real weight. Compare its open left adjoint to the prescribed open shriek by uniqueness of adjoints; preservation transports through that natural isomorphism.

source.place: Final three paragraphs: finite clopen reconstruction, open-closed localization, backward gluing and reduction.

proof.text: Apply Weil-heart localization to each complementary pair. Compare the two open left adjoints and the two closed right adjoints by adjoint uniqueness. Their counit and unit equations give an isomorphism of short complexes; thus the actual prescribed open counit and chosen normalized closed unit give the asserted short exact sequence. The same localization lemma makes every sheaf on the final empty closed member zero.

source.place: Final three paragraphs: finite clopen reconstruction, open-closed localization, backward gluing and reduction.

proof.text: The common-stage compositor is Frobenius-equivariant by the normalized-compositor lemma. The already proved IsoAlgebra.mapOfNatIsoCompIsoOfIso lifts it to Weil pairs; full-subcategory restriction gives the Weil-heart composition isomorphism. Use it to identify all iterated restrictions in the given frontier, respecting ambient_next.

source.place: Final three paragraphs: finite clopen reconstruction, open-closed localization, backward gluing and reduction.

proof.text: For any common bound w choose finite mono-chain presentations of the mixed restrictions on the clopen pieces, and choose the pure quotient weights appearing in these presentations. Apply the prescribed clopen filtration theorem to each open difference. Its common-bound clause proves that the open restriction is mixed of weights at most w, including an empty component set.

source.place: Final three paragraphs: finite clopen reconstruction, open-closed localization, backward gluing and reduction.

proof.text: Induct backwards through the finite closed chain from the empty last member. At each stage the preceding open restriction is mixed and the next closed restriction is mixed by induction. Exact open extension and closed image preserve their bounds. Apply the proved extension clause SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost.of_mono_cokernel to the localization mono; its cokernel is isomorphic to the third term by the cokernel universal property. This proves mixedness at that closed stage.

source.place: Final three paragraphs: finite clopen reconstruction, open-closed localization, backward gluing and reduction.

proof.text: The first closed ambient inclusion is surjective: its composite description is an isomorphism followed by the nilradical immersion, which is surjective by reduction universal homeomorphism. Immersion/reduction filtration transport makes its actual unit invertible. Push the bounded mixed filtration on the first closed stage forward and transport it along the inverse unit to F. Finally choose the initially unspecified bounds on the finitely many pieces and bound their finite range in the real numbers. Enlarging a bound preserves the same finite filtration, giving the existential mixedness assertion as well as every specified common bound.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q58-378db8424 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes. This re-split follows the released note (stage 1, keep_plan, batch 5). The live node still carries the old 7-step proof, so the delivery is not superseded. The statement and stmt_deps are identical to the base. I checked by script that all 7 old steps appear verbatim in the report, and each is now stated by a new node. Old steps 1 and 3 go to lem-zl-weil-heart-localization-exact: subschemes stay separated finite type and Noetherian, the Weil heart is abelian with kernels and cokernels created by the forgetful functor, restriction and i_* are exact, and the actual counit/unit give a short exact sequence, including the empty cases. Old steps 2 and 7 go to lem-zl-immersion-filtered-reduction-transport: j_! and i_* carry a filtration to its image filtration with the same weights, and for a surjective closed immersion the unit is a Weil isomorphism and η^{-1}(e_*G) is the filtration. Old step 5 goes to lem-zl-clopen-prescribed-weil-filtration, and old steps 4 and 6 go to lem-zl-exact-functor-tower-filtration-splicing in abstract abelian form, with weight classes that T_a preserves. The four statements are comparable in size (1988, 2311, 1863 and 1961 characters), and the assembly is 2090 characters in 4 cited steps. Mathematical checks: all four statements are true. The clopen node holds because H ≅ ⊕ h_{b!}h_b^*H. The tower node follows by induction using π^{-1}(TL_s)/π^{-1}(TL_{s-1}) ≅ T(L_s/L_{s-1}). For the transport node, a surjective closed immersion is a nilimmersion, so the unit is an isomorphism. I tested empty pieces, N=0, t=0, the zero functor, a non-split Jordan extension, two points with different weights, F_q[ε]/ε², and V_0=∅. Assembly: step 1 uses the composition isomorphisms that prop-weil-operations states as Weil morphisms. Step 3 applies the tower node with H_t=0 because Z_t=∅, and the transport node gives preservation of purity. Step 4 is exactly the mixedness definition in def-weil-punctual-weights. Checked against the source: main-20261015 thm-zl-real-mixed-by-curves.proof.md, paragraphs 6–9. The reduction goes through empty-complement localization at common-stage Q̄_ℓ, as on the base, not through i-topology (sec-trace-formula). The whole-DAG duplicate search (lem-zl-open-closed-weight, def-weil-open-closed-recollement, prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages, lem-sf-open-closed-weil-mate-structures, lemma-constructible-universal-homeomorphism-invariance, i-topology, lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand) found no duplicate. Form checks pass: statement-only nodes, defined notions, correct created/blueprint fields with via=[item], five searches each, no SGA. Batch-5 finding: the 3 new citations of def-weil-punctual-weights are accepted. It is the general definition of punctual weights and mixedness, it reaches def-weil-local-frobenius-trace only as a definition, and it is not a step of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality proofs; it was already a base stmt_dep of the item. The tool_use prop-weil-operations (generic composition isomorphisms as Weil morphisms) is unchanged from the base and accepted.

lean.statement: theorem zlReducedFrontierMixedGluing (iota : Ω ≃+* ℂ) (C : ZlReducedFrontier D X) (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl X Ω) (mixed : ∀ (a : Fin C.length) (b : Fin (C.count a)), ∃ w : ℝ, SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω (C.piece a b) iota ((zlWeilPull D l hl Ω (C.pieceInclusion a b ≫ C.openInclusion a ≫ C.ambient a.castSucc)).obj F) w) : ∃ (images : ∀ a : Fin C.length, ZlFrontierClosedImage D l hl Ω iota (C.inclusion a)) (reduction : ZlFrontierClosedImage D l hl Ω iota (C.ambient 0)), (∃ w : ℝ, SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω X iota F w) ∧ (∀ w : ℝ, (∀ (a : Fin C.length) (b : Fin (C.count a)), SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω (C.piece a b) iota ((zlWeilPull D l hl Ω (C.pieceInclusion a b ≫ C.openInclusion a ≫ C.ambient a.castSucc)).obj F) w) → SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω X iota F w) ∧ (∀ (a : Fin C.length) (b : Fin (C.count a)), ZlFrontierFiltrationPreservation D l hl Ω iota (zlOpenWeilShriek D l hl Ω (C.pieceInclusion a b))) ∧ (∀ a : Fin C.length, ZlFrontierFiltrationPreservation D l hl Ω iota (zlOpenWeilShriek D l hl Ω (C.openInclusion a)) ∧ ZlFrontierLocalization D l hl Ω iota (C.openInclusion a) (C.inclusion a) (images a) ((zlWeilPull D l hl Ω (C.ambient a.castSucc)).obj F)) ∧ IsIso (reduction.adjunction.unit.app F)
